The user reports they “don’t see it” and shows a screenshot (presumably of the Issues UI missing the new toolbar actions). From earlier context, I was trying to implement a new “Cancel all open tasks” button in the Issues list UI of Paperclip. I’ve already added the toolbarActions slot, button, dialog, and mutation code in the repository under `paperclip/ui`. The code compiles, but the running development server (served on port 3100) is still showing the old UI, because the built assets being served are from the installed npm package `@paperclipai/server/ui-dist` rather than the local `ui/dist` directory. The earlier investigation confirmed that the UI bundle is served from `/home/lane/.npm/_npx/43414d9b790239bb/node_modules/@paperclipai/server/ui-dist`. The local source code lives in `/home/lane/paperclip/ui`. I built the UI with `pnpm build` and saw the build succeeded, producing a `dist` folder with the new assets. However, the server is still loading the previously installed UI-dist, so the changes aren’t reflected.

To get the new UI visible without reinstalling the whole package, I need to replace the contents of the server’s UI distribution directory with the freshly built `dist`. But I should be careful not to lose the existing assets in case something goes wrong, so I’ll back them up first. The backup can be a copy of the current `ui-dist` directory with a timestamp suffix. Then I’ll delete the old `ui-dist` and copy the new `ui/dist` over it. Finally, I’ll list a few files in the `assets` subdirectory to verify the copy succeeded.

Thus, the next step is to run a Bash command that:
1. Shows what’s currently in the local `ui/dist` (for sanity).
2. Backs up the existing server UI-dist directory (`$D`) to `$D.bak-<timestamp>`.
3. Removes the old `$D`.
4. Copies the newly built `ui/dist` into `$D`.
5. Lists a few files in `$D/assets` to confirm the assets are present.

This aligns with the needed action to make the UI changes visible to the user, addressing the “I don’t see it” complaint. I’ll construct the command accordingly and invoke the Bash tool.

arguments.command: ls /home/lane/paperclip/ui/dist | head; D=/home/lane/.npm/_npx/43414d9b790239bb/node_modules/@paperclipai/server/ui-dist; cp -r $D ${D}.bak-$(date +%s) && rm -rf $D && cp -r /home/lane/paperclip/ui/dist $D && ls $D/assets | head -3
arguments.description: Swap built UI into installed package (backup first)
